newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-WINGS BEAT CANADIENS TO STRETCH STREAK.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-WINGS BEAT CANADIENS TO STRETCH STREAK.

text.p: Vyacheslav Kozlov, Sergei Fedorov, Darren McCarty and Steve Yzerman each tallied a goal and an assist to lead the Detroit Red Wings to a 5-3 win over the Montreal Canadiens Wednesday.
The win extended Detroit's unbeaten streak to six while Montreal remained winless on the road this season (0-4).

"We try to preach defence and hold teams to a low-scoring game," said Martin Lapointe, who scored Detroit's first goal. "Tonight, they got three goals, so it was good for us to have a night when everybody was scoring."
In Dallas, Andy Moog made 24 saves for his second shutout of the season and Benoit Hogue and Greg Adams scored third-period goals to lead the Dallas Stars to a 2-0 blanking of the Buffalo Sabres.
Moog, the league's oldest active netminder at 36, stopped three shots in the first period, 13 in the second and eight in the third for the 24th shutout of his 16-year career.
The victory was the 332nd of Moog's career, tying him with Harry Lumley for seventh on the all-time list.

At Colorado, Adam Deadmarsh and Peter Forsberg scored within a two-minute span of a four-goal second period to boost the Colorado Avalanche to their fourth straight win, a 6-3 defeat of the St. Louis Blues.

The Blues took a 2-1 lead into the second period, but Deadmarsh scored the first of his two goals, a power-play marker just 24 seconds into the frame, to tie the score and Forsberg added the go-ahead goal, his sixth of the season, at 2:12 to give Colorado the lead for good.
At Florida, Mike Hough's goal with 2:17 left snapped a tie as the Florida Panthers extended their unbeaten streak to 12 games with a 3-2 defeat of the Chicago Blackhawks.

Tied at 2-2, Ed Jovanovski slid a pass to Tom Fitzgerald, who skated to the right faceoff circle. Fitzgerald rifled a low wrist shot that goaltender Ed Belfour stopped, but the rebound bounced right to Hough, who shoveled a backhand shot between the pads of the Chicago goalie.
"After last night (a road tie against the New York Rangers), we didn't have very strong legs but we refused to lose," Hough said. "We have enough ties and didn't want another overtime."
In Hartford, Kevin Dineen's power-play goal 4:43 into the third period lifted the Hartford Whalers to a 2-2 tie with the New York Islanders.

With New York's Randy Wood serving a hooking penalty, Dineen took a pass from Andrew Cassels at the top of the right faceoff circle and fired a slap shot through the pads of goaltender Eric Fichaud for his fifth goal of the season.
"We sure didn't play very well," Dineen said. "We actually played very badly. I think we all realised it in time and we went out and played the third period a lot better than the first."

At New Jersey, Brian Leetch scored a pair of power-play goals, rookie Daniel Goneau tallied twice and Mike Richter made 53 saves to pace the New York Rangers to a 6-1 victory over the New Jersey Devils.

Leetch's third goal of the season and first of the game at 7:30 gave the Rangers an early cushion. Darren Langdon added his initial tally of the campaign just over eight minutes later to double the lead.
In Ottawa, Daniel Alfredsson's power-play goal midway through the third period lifted Ottawa to a 2-2 tie with the Los Angeles Kings and kept the Senators unbeaten at home.
Alfredsson scored at 9:29 of the third when he received Alexei Yashin's pass from behind the net and lifted the puck over goaltender Stephane Fiset, who made 29 saves.

In Washington, Jason Allison scored with 1:48 left in the third period to snap a tie, lifting the Washington Capitals to a 4-2 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers, who have lost three straight games.

Steve Konowalchuk had a breakaway but lost the puck in the Philadelphia zone. Todd Krygier raced to the puck in the right corner and passed to Allison, who snapped a wrist shot through goaltender Garth Snow's pads for his team-leading fifth goal and a 3-2 advantage.
In Anaheim, Trevor Linden scored his first two goals of the season as the Vancouver Canucks defeated the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 6-3, spoiling the season's debut of Paul Kariya.
Linden's first goal, a power-play marker, gave Vancouver the lead for good at 3-2 with 7:22 left in the second period.
Kariya, who scored a franchise-record 50 goals last season, was held scoreless after missing the first 11 games with an inflammed abdominal muscle.
In Edmonton, Ryan Smyth scored two goals and Doug Weight added three assists as the Edmonton Oilers defeated the slumping Phoenix Coyotes, 4-1.
The win was the Oilers third in four games and second over the Coyotes this season. Phoenix has dropped three of four and hasn't posted consecutive wins since October 10th-12th.
In 12 games this season, Smyth has surpassed his totals for last season when he had two goals and added nine assists in 48 games.

In San Jose, Owen Nolan continued his torrid play with two goals, and Kelly Hrudey stopped 23 shots as the San Jose Sharks posted a 3-1 victory over the Calgary Flames, snapping their five-game unbeaten streak.
Nolan had a power-play goal in the second period to knot the game and sealed the victory with an empty-net tally in the final seconds. He has seven goals in his last four games.
